title: Torsion subsheaf and torsion-free quotient
statement: Let $X$ be an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] with generic point $\eta$, and let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. The local sections whose image in $\mathcal F_\eta$ is zero form a quasi-coherent submodule $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{tors}}\subseteq\mathcal F$. At each $x\in X$ its stalk is the torsion submodule of $\mathcal F_x$ over the domain $\mathcal O_{X,x}$, and the quotient $\mathcal F/\mathcal F_{\mathrm{tors}}$ is torsion-free. Equivalently, $\mathcal F_{\mathrm{tors}}$ is the kernel of the natural map $\mathcal F\to j_*\mathcal F_\eta$, where $j:\operatorname{Spec}k(X)\to X$ is the generic-point morphism and $k(X)$ is its function field [def-sc-function-field]. Here torsion in a stalk means annihilation by a nonzero element of the domain $\mathcal O_{X,x}$, and torsion-free means having no nonzero torsion element.

proof.text: For every open $U\subseteq X$, let $\mathcal T(U)$ be the sections whose generic germ is zero. The equivalence in [lem-sc-torsion-sections-generic] identifies these with torsion sections and shows stability under restriction and multiplication, so they form a submodule $\mathcal T\subseteq\mathcal F$. This is the sectionwise kernel of $\mathcal F\to j_*\mathcal F_\eta$. The generic-point morphism is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so [pqf-lem-pushforward-qcoh] makes $j_*\mathcal F_\eta$ quasi-coherent; [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel] then makes $\mathcal T$ quasi-coherent.

For $x\in X$, $\mathcal T_x\subseteq\mathcal F_x$ by [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact] (1), and a germ in $\mathcal T_x$ is represented by a section $s$ on a neighbourhood of $x$ whose generic germ is zero, so [lem-sc-torsion-sections-generic] says that it is killed by a nonzero element of the domain $\mathcal O_{X,x}$. Conversely, if a germ of $\mathcal F_x$ is killed by a nonzero local element, represent it by a section on a neighbourhood and apply [lem-sc-torsion-sections-generic] after shrinking to the neighbourhood on which the annihilation equation holds; the germ then lies in $\mathcal T_x$. Thus $\mathcal T_x$ is exactly the torsion submodule of $\mathcal F_x$.

Let $q:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F/\mathcal T$ be the quotient (the cokernel of $\mathcal T\subseteq\mathcal F$); it is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image] (2), and by [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact] (3) $q_y$ induces $(\mathcal F/\mathcal T)_y\cong\mathcal F_y/\mathcal T_y$ for every $y\in X$. Let $x\in X$ and let $\bar s\in(\mathcal F/\mathcal T)_x$ be killed by a nonzero $a\in\mathcal O_{X,x}$. Represent $\bar s$ by a section $\sigma$ of $\mathcal F/\mathcal T$ on an open $V\ni x$ and, using the surjection $\mathcal F_x\to(\mathcal F/\mathcal T)_x$, choose (after shrinking $V$) $s\in\mathcal F(V)$ with $q(s)=\sigma$. As $\sigma_x$ is torsion, [lem-sc-torsion-sections-generic] applied to the quasi-coherent $\mathcal F/\mathcal T$ gives $\sigma_\eta=0$. Since $\mathcal T_\eta=0$ (a germ at $\eta$ of a section with zero generic germ is zero), $(\mathcal F/\mathcal T)_\eta=\mathcal F_\eta$, so $s_\eta=0$, i.e. $s\in\mathcal T(V)$ and $\sigma=q(s)=0$, whence $\bar s=0$. Thus the quotient is torsion-free.

lean.statement: theorem torsion_subsheaf_quotient (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X] (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] : ∃ (T : X.Modules) (i : T ⟶ F), Mono i ∧ T.IsQuasicoherent ∧ (∀ (U : X.Opens) (s : Γ(F, U)), (∃ t : Γ(T, U), i.app U t = s) ↔ ∀ hη : genericPoint X ∈ U, F.presheaf.germ U (genericPoint X) hη s = 0) ∧ (∀ (x : X) (s : F.presheaf.stalk x), s ∈ Set.range (i.stalkLinearMap x) ↔ ∃ a : X.presheaf.stalk x, a ≠ 0 ∧ a • s = 0) ∧ (∀ (x : X) (s : (cokernel i).presheaf.stalk x) (a : X.presheaf.stalk x), a ≠ 0 → a • s = 0 → s = 0) ∧ ∃ h : i ≫ toSkyscraper (LinearMap.id : F.presheaf.stalk (genericPoint X) →ₗ[X.functionField] F.presheaf.stalk (genericPoint X)) = 0, Nonempty (IsLimit (KernelFork.ofι i h))
